strings.name: Jim Keller
strings.summary: Jim Keller has worked on processor projects at DEC, AMD, Apple and Tesla, spanning general computing, mobile devices and automotive hardware. He now leads Tenstorrent; chip architecture, software and manufacturing achievements involve many engineers and teams.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth year is unconfirmed. Appointment announcements and start dates, funding and revenue, and partnership plans and completed deployments are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Contributed to successive high-performance processor designs, advancing chip architectures and computing platforms across companies.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: BS in electrical engineering from Penn State University; no unverified graduation year is supplied here.
strings.facts.f2.label: Technical work
strings.facts.f2.value: Co-authored the x86-64 instruction set and HyperTransport specification, and worked on mobile chips and automotive hardware.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Processor design across generations
strings.highlights.h1.text: Held architecture and design leadership roles across companies, including AMD Zen and Apple A4/A5; entire chip generations are not credited to one person.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Leading an AI computing company
strings.highlights.h2.text: Moved from Tenstorrent president and CTO to CEO, advancing AI computing systems and CPU intellectual-property business.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Company announces self-hosted AI partnership
strings.timeline.t1.text: Tenstorrent and ConfidentialMind announce platform validation and joint sales plans; this is company teamwork, not completed global deployment.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Company announces Series E funding
strings.timeline.t2.text: Tenstorrent reports closing $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion post-money valuation. Keller comments on its computing architecture; neither funding nor valuation is operating revenue.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes Tenstorrent CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: Exchanges roles with former CEO Ljubisa Bajic, who becomes CTO; this historical arrangement does not assert that Bajic still holds that job.
strings.timeline.t4.title: President and CTO appointment announced
strings.timeline.t4.text: Tenstorrent announces Keller as president, CTO and board member; the announcement date does not establish when any earlier collaboration began.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Resigns from Intel
strings.timeline.t5.text: Intel says he resigns for personal reasons, effective that day, and agrees to six months of transition consulting.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Starts new Intel role
strings.timeline.t6.text: Becomes senior vice president leading silicon engineering; the appointment was announced April 26, after work in Tesla automotive hardware.
strings.timeline.t7.title: AMD announces his return
strings.timeline.t7.text: Becomes corporate vice president and chief architect of microprocessor cores, focusing on high-performance and low-power core design.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Apple acquires P.A. Semi
strings.timeline.t8.text: His career includes P.A. Semi and Apple; the acquisition year is distinct from his personal job-change date.
